system_description.narrative_title: Escalating Russia–Ukraine war: strikes, air-defence shortages, global spillovers
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an intensification of the Russia–Ukraine conflict driven by sustained missile and drone strikes, targeted attacks on economic infrastructure, and growing shortages in Western air-defence supplies. As an open system, the conflict links military operations, logistics (weapons, air-defence systems), political stability in Kyiv, international diplomatic/military support flows, and global economic nodes (energy and food). Feedback loops — depleted Patriot stocks reducing protection, attacks on economic targets provoking wider escalation, and domestic political turnover in Ukraine affecting strategy and external aid — amplify instability and produce cross-border consequences.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary are active military strike campaigns (missiles, drones, air attacks), Ukrainian defence capacity and political leadership, NATO and allied arms/diplomatic support flows (including Patriot supply chains), attacks on critical infrastructure and supply chains (energy, logistics, food), and the resulting civilian casualties, displacement, and domestic political reactions.
system_description.super_system: Euro‑Atlantic security architecture and the global economic system (energy and food markets, trade and logistics)
adjacent_subsystems: Western defense‑industrial supply chain (Patriot missiles, munitions, drone countermeasures)
European energy and gas infrastructure (pipelines, terminals, regional projects)
Global food and agricultural supply chains

variables.name: Strike campaign intensity
variables.description: The aggregate rate and scale of long-range and unmanned strike operations (missile, drone, air) over time.

variables.name: Air‑defense availability
variables.description: The operational inventory and readiness of active air‑defense systems and intercept capacity.

variables.name: External arms supply rate
variables.description: The tempo at which external military equipment and munitions are delivered into the conflict system.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure damage
variables.description: The accumulated physical degradation or loss of key economic and logistics infrastructure (energy, transport, storage).

variables.name: Energy market disruption
variables.description: The degree of disturbance in energy production, transport, pricing and supply chains affecting markets beyond the conflict zone.

variables.name: Food supply disruption
variables.description: The extent to which agricultural production, storage and export channels are impaired, altering food availability and prices.

variables.name: Logistics resilience
variables.description: The capacity of military and commercial logistics networks to sustain supply flows under attack and disruption.

variables.name: Civilian casualty rate
variables.description: The ongoing rate of non‑combatant deaths and injuries resulting from military operations and strikes.

variables.name: Displacement level
variables.description: The cumulative number of people uprooted or relocated due to insecurity and infrastructure loss.

variables.name: Political leadership stability
variables.description: The perceived and operational stability of executive and strategic political leadership affecting decision continuity.

variables.name: Escalation pressure
variables.description: The tendency for conflict dynamics to intensify, measured by reciprocal targeting, provocative actions and triggers for broader use of force.

variables.name: Air‑defense replenishment rate
variables.description: The rate at which air‑defense systems and associated munitions are procured, manufactured, transferred and fielded to restore intercept capacity.

variables.name: Command and control status
variables.description: The integrity and functionality of military command, control and communications networks enabling coordinated operations.

variables.name: Trade and logistics disruption
variables.description: The degree to which international trade routes, ports and freight networks are impaired, delaying or rerouting commercial flows.

variables.name: International support sentiment
variables.description: The prevailing attitudes and willingness among external audiences and decision makers to provide diplomatic, material or political support.

variables.name: Cumulative economic cost
variables.description: The aggregated economic burden from direct damages, lost output and market disruption attributable to the conflict over time.

catalysts.title: France accelerates air‑defence deliveries
catalysts.description: French pledge to speed air‑defence shipments to Ukraine will raise incoming intercept capacity and speed up replenishment of depleted stocks.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'France agrees to accelerate air defence deliveries to Ukraine, Zelenskiy says'

catalysts.title: Franco‑British‑German co‑chair meeting (Mon)
catalysts.description: Leaders meeting to co‑chair Ukraine session could fast‑track coordinated political and material support decisions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'French, British, German leaders to co-chair meeting on Ukraine on Monday'

catalysts.title: Russian mobilisation of ~300,000 after elections
catalysts.description: Statements and readiness tests point to large‑scale Russian draft and force expansion after September elections, raising fighting capacity and tensions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Putin will draft 300,000 new troops after September elections, Zelenskiy says' and 'Russia Tests Readiness for New Round of Military Mobilization'

catalysts.title: Sustained Russian missile and drone assaults
catalysts.description: Ongoing high‑tempo Russian strikes on Ukrainian population and infrastructure are likely to continue in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia launches deadly missile and drone attacks on Kyiv', 'Russian strikes kill 17 in Ukraine', 'Russian 'double-tap' strike on shopping centre kills 16'

catalysts.title: Ukraine attacks Russian energy and logistics sites
catalysts.description: Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, terminals and warehouses indicate an intensifying campaign targeting economic and logistics nodes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine hits Russia's TANECO oil refinery, oil terminal', 'Ukrainian drones hit Ozon warehouse/Orenburg warehouse'

catalysts.title: Depletion of Patriot munitions / launcher shortages
catalysts.description: Reports that Patriot launchers are running empty imply near‑term reduced intercept capacity until replenishments arrive.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine left exposed as Patriot launchers run empty', 'Dwindling Patriot Supplies Leave Kyiv in the Line of Fire'

catalysts.title: Private‑sector targeting assistance (Musk/tech)
catalysts.description: Ukraine solicits Elon Musk's help to strike missile launchers; private commercial tech or targeting support could increase strike effectiveness.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine seeks Musk’s help to hit Russian missile launchers' (repeated)

catalysts.title: Norway pledge: >$9bn to Ukraine in 2027
catalysts.description: A large, scheduled Norwegian financial package in 2027 will bolster international support and resource availability next year.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Norway to give over $9 billion to Ukraine in 2027'

catalysts.title: Attacks/incidents near European gas projects
catalysts.description: Drone and marine drone incidents near critical gas projects (e.g., Neptun Deep, Neptun/Neptun Deep, Romania) raise regional energy security and trade disruption risks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Romania scrambles F-16 to destroy drone near critical European gas project', 'Romania destroys marine drone near Neptun Deep gas project'

catalysts.title: Ousted Ukrainian defence minister's US funding trip
catalysts.description: Planned US trip by Ukraine's ousted defence minister to raise project funding could influence external support flows and domestic political stability.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Ukraine's ousted defence minister plans US trip to raise project funding'
